description: How much more it cost to produce low-emissions ammonia than conventional ammonia from unabated natural gas in the European Union in 2024, as the IEA states it: around 25 percent more with carbon capture and about 120 to 220 percent more from electrolysis; as little as 5 percent and 75 to 160 percent more if a CO2 cost of USD 100 per tonne applied.

processing.description: Read the text of the PDF (sha256 94f2912332e1…). Found each of the 2 quoted statement(s) word for word on PDF page(s) 53, and the 3 context sentence(s) the scope relies on, before publishing.

Published each number exactly as printed, with its statement in the value's note. A range 'A-B%' is published as its low end A and high end B (dimension 'bound'); nothing was computed, rounded or combined with any other source.
'As little as 5%' is published as the stated value 5 for carbon capture with a CO2 cost of USD 100 per tonne; the sentence gives no other figure for that case.

scope.basis: Ammonia made with carbon capture or by electrolysis, compared with conventional (unabated natural gas-based) ammonia. Levelised cost of production in 2024 (the text's present tense, matching Figure 2.9, 'Levelised cost of production of selected materials by technology, 2024'), IEA analysis. Energy costs are regional end-user prices for industry including taxes and charges; no explicit financial support, though support embedded in cost components (such as fossil fuel subsidies) may be included (figure note). The 'with a CO2 cost' values assume USD 100 per tonne of CO2, the figure's carbon tax case.
